title: Activation Blueprint: Fieldwork Sprint & Eval Rubric
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, execution-first activation blueprint for customer POCs where we need fast field validation (14 days) followed by a gated decision to proceed to Dedicated/Production. Emphasis: measurable acceptance criteria, minimal infra friction, and explicit fall-through options if latency/cost/accuracy don't meet thresholds.

Scope and when to use this doc:
- Use for commercial POCs that are: (a) model/serving validation, (b) end-to-end inference latency & cost profiling, or (c) feature validation (chat/assistant, reranking, embeddings).
- Not for sustained performance benchmarking or training/DataScience-only experiments.

Primary outcomes (14 days):
1) Functional baseline: sample app responds correctly for canonical flows (chat + tool call or batch embed).
2) SLO report: measured p50/p95 token latency, tokens/sec throughput, and per-request cost estimate.
3) Quality check: automated eval on 200 representative prompts + 50 human-reviewed samples with pass/fail rubric.
4) Operational readiness: CI smoke test, monitoring hooks, and simple rollback plan.
5) Go/no-go decision with a prioritized list of follow-on items.

Roles & accountability:
- SE Lead: owns workshop, runbook, and decision matrix (Evelyn Soto).
- Customer Eng: coordinates test data and app integration.
- Infra: creates temporary Dedicated instance or service tokens, ensures network access.
- Product/PM: validates success metric relevance.

Pre-work checklist (customer + Redwood, completed before Day 0):
- Customer: provide 200 representative prompts (CSV), schema for input/output, and contact for network allowlist.
- Redwood: provide API key, minimal SDK example, and test harness repo.
- Shared: agree on privacy/PII redaction approach for logs.

Day-by-day fieldwork sprint (high-level):
- Day 0 (kickoff, 90m): alignment on scope, walk test harness, assign owners, confirm data set and access. Agenda: context (10m), acceptance rubric (20m), integration plan (30m), risks & fallbacks (20m), next actions.
- Day 1–3: integration + smoke-run. Connect sample app, validate model pulls, run small-scale load (50 reqs). Capture errors, latency distribution.
- Day 4–7: instrumentation & baseline measurement. Run 3x 30-minute windows: peak, steady, cold-start. Collect p50/p95 token latency, server saw queue times, KV cache hit rate if enabled.
- Day 8–10: quality eval. Run automated eval harness, then schedule 2-hour human review session for edge-cases.
- Day 11–12: cost modeling & optimizations. Try small quantized variant / batching changes, measure delta in cost/latency.
- Day 13: consolidate results into SLO report and decision matrix.
- Day 14: final review + go/no-go meeting (45m). Decision captured in ticket and next-phase plan agreed.

Decision matrix & acceptance rubric (must pass to proceed):
- Functional pass: 95% of sample flows succeed end-to-end (no crash, proper schema) -> pass/fail.
- Latency guardrails: p95 request token latency <= 800ms OR documented tradeoff (if customer tolerates higher latency).
- Throughput: baseline sustained throughput must match or exceed the customer target within 20% (e.g., target 50 qps => measured sustained >= 40 qps).
- Cost envelope: estimated per-1k-request cost within 30% of target budget or a committed optimization path exists.
- Quality: automated eval score above baseline threshold (we set threshold per-customer; default: BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity >= 0.78) OR human review finds <10% critical failure modes.
- Operational: monitoring hooks shipping, synthetic smoke alert configured, and rollback policy documented.

If any of the above fail, the gating outcome options:
- Remediation sprint (7 days) with predefined owner & success targets.
- Roll-forward to a restricted pilot with degraded SLA and cost share.
- Termination with checklist of artifacts (logs, pcap if network issue) for RFC/lessons learned.

Measurement details (how to compute):
- p95 token latency: measure token-output latencies from first user byte to last token arrival; capture at client-side SDK where possible.
- Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec during steady-state window (define steady-state as a 10-minute window after warmup having <10% variance).
- Cost estimate: include inference time, data egress, and any ephemeral infra; compute per-1k-requests normalized to typical prompt length.
- Automated eval: test harness returns pass/fail, confusion matrix, and a short diff for samples that change after optimization.

Workshop agenda (detailed for kickoff):
1) Welcome & introductions (10m)
2) Objective framing: 14-day outcomes and decision criteria (10m)
3) Product walkthrough: API/variants, token accounting, monitoring endpoints (20m)
4) Integration plan: repo, test harness, data handoff, access (20m)
5) Risk register: GDPR/PII, latency hotspots, quota ceilings (15m)
6) Quick demo: run a canonical flow live (10m)
7) Next steps & ownerships (5m)

Risk register (top-of-mind & mitigations):
- Data availability: customer delays in providing prompts -> mitigation: use synthetic fallback and focus on latency/infra metrics first.
- Network allowlist: blocked egress -> mitigation: ask infra to provide VPN jumpbox; plan for Private deployment if required.
- Model mismatch: customer expects hallucination-free output -> mitigation: set conservative quality gates and propose reranking layer.
- Cost surprises: spikes in token consumption -> mitigation: enable quota and rate-limiting, create budget alert.

Deliverables at decision meeting:
- 1-page SLO & cost summary (p50/p95/throughput/cost per-1k)
- Eval summary (automated + top 10 human edge cases)
- Action log with owners and timeframe for remediation or next phase
- Final recommendation (go to Dedicated / pilot / stop) and rationale

Notes to SEs (practical tips):
- Prefer client-side timing for latency SLOs to measure real user experience.
- For embeddings workloads, sample 1k pairs to compute recall metrics; surface nearest-neighbor drift after quantization.
- When in doubt, prioritize reproducible tests (CI job that can rerun the 14-day baseline).
- Keep the customer engaged: weekly 15m sync + shared dashboard link.

Quick checklist (copyable for template):
- [ ] Kickoff scheduled and invite sent
- [ ] Customer test data received (200 prompts)
- [ ] API key + SDK sample confirmed working
- [ ] Baseline 3x measurement windows executed
- [ ] Automated eval completed
- [ ] Human review session recorded and notes taken
- [ ] Cost calc and optimization notes added
- [ ] Decision meeting scheduled

Appendix: sample go/no-go decision text (to paste into ticket):
"Recommendation: Proceed to pilot with Dedicated capacity. Rationale: Functional baseline met (98% pass), p95 token latency 640ms (under 800ms), throughput target met (45 qps sustained on 50 qps target), embedding similarity 0.81, estimated per-1k-request cost within 15% of budget. Remediations: 1) Add prefix caching to reduce cold-start tokens by 12% (owner: Infra), 2) Run quantization candidate in staging (owner: SE)."
